definition: The random and spontaneous change of an unstable nucleus into a more stable form, with the emission of alpha, beta or gamma radiation; its rate is not affected by temperature, pressure or chemical state.
A particle of 2 protons and 2 neutrons, the same as a helium-4 nucleus, with charge $+2e$; strongly ionising and stopped by a sheet of paper.
Radioactive decay in which a nucleus emits an alpha particle, so its proton number falls by 2 and its nucleon number by 4.
Radioactive decay in which a neutron in the nucleus changes into a proton, emitting an electron and an antineutrino; the proton number rises by 1 and the nucleon number is unchanged.
Radioactive decay in which a proton in the nucleus changes into a neutron, emitting a positron and a neutrino; the proton number falls by 1 and the nucleon number is unchanged.
The emission of a gamma photon when a nucleus in an excited state drops to a lower energy level; the proton number and nucleon number do not change.
An uncharged particle with a very small mass, emitted with a positron in beta-plus decay; it interacts with matter so rarely that it is very hard to detect.
The antiparticle of the neutrino: uncharged, with a very small mass, and emitted with an electron in beta-minus decay.
The removal of electrons from atoms or molecules to form ions; alpha particles cause the most ionisation along their path and gamma rays the least.
